title: רב זירא
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness
attribution: Fresh project English, authored from the frozen Hebrew and revised through source-informed author and independent model review. Editorial-layer attribution in the Warsaw witness remains qualified.

paragraphs: A) He is Rabbi Zeira: after they ordained him in the Land of Israel he was called Rabbi. Previously he did not want ordination; end of Ketubbot. He erred: the end of Ketubbot says nothing about ordination. Rather, Sanhedrin chapter 1, 14: Rabbi Zeira hid to avoid ordination, for Rabbi Elazar said, “Be obscure and endure.” When he heard Rabbi Elazar’s statement that no one rises to greatness unless his sins are forgiven, he presented himself. When they ordained him, they sang: “No eye paint, no rouge, no coiffure, yet a graceful gazelle,” there, and Ketubbot 17a. Jerusalem Talmud, last chapter of Bikkurim,halakhah 3: they wanted to appoint Rabbi Zeira, and he would not accept. When he heard the teaching that attaining high standing brings atonement for a sage, a bridegroom and a patriarch, he accepted appointment. In Ketubbot 43,beginning of side b: Rav Zeira said: Rav Mattanah said in Rav’s name; some say Rabbi Zeira said: Rav Mattanah said in Rav’s name. Rashi writes: in Babylonia, before he went up to the Land of Israel before Rabbi Yochanan, he was called Rav Zeira, since ordination does not take place in Babylonia. After going up and receiving ordination he was Rabbi Zeira; Rashi likewise writes in Moed Katan 25b. One says he stated it before ordination. End of quotation. But Tosafot, Menachot 40b, on the linen sheet that Beit Shammai exempts from tzitzit: Rava said, “I stated this matter, and in the West it was stated in Rabbi Zeira’s name like me: perhaps his sheet will tear and he will sew it, whereas the Torah said ‘make,’ not from what is already made.” Rabbi Zeira—a scribal error for Rav Zeira, as in Beit Yosef, Orach Chayim,section 9—said it is also a decree concerning a night garment. Tosafot writes, “Rabbi Zeira”—it should read Rav Zeira—“said, ‘A decree …,’ implying that Rav Zeira is not Rabbi Zeira, unlike Rashi’s explanation in Ketubbot.” End of quotation. But in Rif I saw there, “Rabbah said, ‘A decree …,’” leaving no basis for Tosafot’s proof of two persons. Tosafot did not accept Rashi’s explanation and say that before ordination, when called Rav, he said “a decree,” and after ordination, called Rabbi, he said “perhaps it will tear,” because then the arranger should have reversed them, first Rav Zeira’s words, then Rabbi Zeira’s.

B) Rabbi Zeira [זעירא] is like Katina, or Rabbi Zeira [זירא] with the ayin absorbed. I did not understand his wording. However, Chiddushei Aggadot, Bava Metzia 85, says that because he was short they called him Keina [קעינא, as printed]. Sefer Yuchasin writes that for this reason he is also called Zeira with an ayin in the Jerusalem Talmud, while the Babylonian Talmud absorbs the ayin. End of quotation. Know that the Jerusalem Talmud calls Rabbi Zeira [זירא] Zeira [זעירא]. The teacher and student whom the Babylonian Talmud associates with Rabbi Zeira you will find with Rabbi Zeira in the Jerusalem Talmud. Likewise, a statement Rabbi Zeira makes in the Babylonian Talmud is made by Rabbi Zeira with an ayin in the Jerusalem Talmud. Beginning of Taanit chapter 2: in Rabbi Zeira’s name; in the Jerusalem Talmud, Rabbi Zeira with an ayin. Berakhot 14a: Rabbi Zeira said, “Whoever sleeps without a dream …”; chapter Haroeh 55b: Rabbi Zeira with an ayin said, “Whoever sleeps ….” Likewise the above statement about hiding from ordination, and many places (see Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak). See Zeira with an ayin; there you will see whether they are the words of Rabbi Zeira or Zeira with an ayin and not Rabbi Zeira [the source’s final distinction is unclear].

C) Yuchasin, under alef, at Rav Pappa’s father, writes that Sefer Kabbalat HaChasid, which explained the Torah portions according to kabbalah, says Rabbi Zeira and Rav Pappa had no known father, like Ben Sira. This is not so: the Talmud mentions their fathers: Rabbi Zeira’s father before Rabbi Zeira; some say “behind Rabbi Zeira”—a scribal error for “Rabbi Zeira’s brother,” see shortly below; see Rav Pappa. At the beginning of Sefer Ben Sira: three were born without intercourse with a husband, Ben Sira, Rav Pappa and Rabbi Zeira. Their mothers once went to the bathhouse; Israelite semen entered their wombs, they conceived and gave birth, without knowing their fathers. Ben Sira’s birth, however, is known; see his entry. But Taanit 26,end of side b, explicitly says Rabbi Zeira’s father objects. In Moed Katan 20b: Issi, Rabbi Zeira’s father—some say his brother—before Rabbi Zeira. Shabbat 121,end of side b: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said, “Lamps ….” Rabbi Zeira asked, “Carried in one hand or two?” He answered, “Like those of your father’s house.” Rabbi Abba said, “In twenty wagons …”; Rabbi Zeira asked, “Carried by one person …?” He answered, “Like those of your father’s house.” In Chullin 46a, troops came to Pumbedita; Rabbah and Rav Yosef fled. Rabbi Zeira met them and said, “Fugitives! The olive-sized amount they spoke of is at the gallbladder.” Tosafot writes that Rabbi Zeira did not have to flee, because his father was the king’s collector, as stated in chapter Zeh Borer, 25,end of side b: he was collector for thirteen years. When the river-chief came to town and he saw rabbis, he told them, “Go, my people, enter your chambers.” See Chelkat Mechokek, Even HaEzer,section 1: regarding a woman who conceived in a bath, whether the father fulfilled procreation and whether the child is his son in every respect. See responsa Beit Yaakov,section 122, that he fulfilled it [כי״ו]. Beit Shmuel brings proof from Semak and Bach, Yoreh Deah 195: a woman should not lie on sheets on which another man lay, lest, heaven forbid, she conceive from semen and the child marry his paternal sister. This implies he is his son in every respect. End of quotation. How, then, did Zeira and Pappa marry wives according to the aforementioned view that their fathers were unknown? Blessed be the Lord, their fathers have been found, as above.

D) He went twice to the Land of Israel: once in Rav Yehudah’s time, as Shabbat 41a and Ketubbot 110,end of side b, say he evaded his teacher Rav Yehudah to go there; see Tosafot,Chullin 13a. Once in Rava’s time. He lived long: Megillah and Taanit (see above,Rav Adda bar Ahavah). So too it appears, for he was also in Rabbi’s time: Avodah Zarah 36b, Rabbi Zeira said, “I had great trouble with Rabbi Assi, Rabbi Assi with Rabbi Yochanan, Rabbi Yochanan with Rabbi Yannai, Rabbi Yannai with Rabbi Natan ben Amram, and Rabbi Natan ben Amram with Rabbi: from when does a Cuthean infant convey impurity? He told me, ‘From one day old.’ When I came to Rabbi Chiyya he said, ‘Nine years old.’ When I came and presented my words to Rabbi, he said, ‘Leave my words and hold Rabbi Chiyya’s.’” Tosafot writes that all were in one generation in Rabbi’s days. Rav Yehudah was born when Rabbi died, and Zeira was Rav Yehudah’s student. Rava was born when Rav Yehudah died; when Zeira was old he addressed Rava as “master,” so Rava was grown. When he asked Rabbi Assi …, presumably he too was grown, and perhaps he asked this several years before Rabbi’s death. Some say Rabbi Chiyya died before Rabbi; when he asked, Chiyya was alive. Thus he would be exceptionally old; perhaps this pressure requires saying there were two. In Recanati and Sh.K.,Behar: Rabbi Shimon the Timnite asked Rabbi Zeira, “I heard you are expert in the chambers of Torah ….” In Otiyyot de-Rabbi Akiva, 11d: “I handed it to Metatron my servant, who handed it to Moses; Moses to Joshua; Joshua to the elders, and then to the prophets, the Great Assembly, Ezra and Hillel in turn; Hillel to Rabbi Abbahu; Abbahu to Zeira; Zeira to men of faith.” End of quotation. It is not puzzling that Rabbi Akiva mentions Abbahu and Zeira in his book, for later people composed the book, as I wrote in the rules. But it is puzzling that Shimon the Timnite was in Akiva’s time, while Zeira was in Rava’s time, nearly 220 years later. When Shimon called him expert in Torah’s chambers, he was presumably grown. This is puzzling unless there were two Zeiras or two Shimons the Timnite. “Hillel to Rabbi Abbahu” also spans many generations. Sefer Elleh Massei, 9,end of side b, cites Midrash HaNeelam,Vayetze 74b: when Zeira came before Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh, Elazar ben Arakh was weeping …. There,column 3: he said to Zeira …. This is puzzling, for Elazar ben Arakh was in Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s days before the destruction. Necessarily there were two or three Rabbi Zeiras.

E) When he went up to the Land of Israel he observed 100 fasts—Maharshal reads forty—to forget the Babylonian learning; another 100, or 40, so Rabbi Elazar would not die in his lifetime and public affairs fall upon him; another 100, or 40, so Gehenna’s fire would not rule him. Every thirty days he tested himself, firing an oven, entering and sitting inside; fire did not rule him. One day the rabbis set their eyes upon him and his legs were scorched. They called him Katina Charikh Shakei, “the short one with scorched legs”—Katina because he was short,Rashi—Bava Metzia 85a. He lit fire in honor of the Sabbath,Shabbat 119a; measure for measure fire did not rule him. Shalshelet HaKabbalah 33b writes: he was very small, accustomed to sitting in a fiery furnace without burning. Some say this came from adjurations; some say he was treated with salamander substance. This appears nonsense: how would that tell him Gehenna’s fire would not rule him? Some say a miracle showed that from his great righteousness Gehenna’s fire would not rule him. End of quotation; this is the truth. Zeira fell ill. Abbahu undertook that if the short one with scorched legs recovered, he would make a feast for the rabbis. He recovered, and Abbahu made a meal and told Zeira, “Let the master begin for us.” He answered, “Does the master not hold that the host breaks bread …?” Berakhot 46,beginning of side a. Violent men lived near Zeira; he drew them close to bring them to repentance. When he died they said, “Until now the scorched short-legged one prayed for us; now who will?” They reflected and repented: Sanhedrin 37a. In Menachot, an angel found him concerning tzitzit, saying, “Katina,Katina,a cloak in winter ….” I do not know who told him the angel spoke to Rabbi Zeira, called Katina Charikh Shakei (see Rav Katina). Perhaps he derived it from his wearing a sheet: Rashi says it had no tzitzit, as above 40b, Rabbi Zeira’s decree for night garments. He therefore thought Katina was Zeira, who had no tzitzit on his sheet. Chullin 122a: Zeira was among Babylonia’s pious. Zeira was sharp and raised objections; Rabbah bar Mattanah was measured and reached conclusions (see his entry). They said to Zeira, “Your teachings are sharp.” He answered, “They are of the daytime”: Eruvin 65a. When exhausted from study he sat at Rabbi Natan bar Tuvyah’s doorway to rise before rabbis and receive reward (see his entry). When weak he sat at Rav Yehudah bar Ammi’s doorway, saying, “I shall rise before rabbis and receive reward”: Eruvin 28b. Rabbi Yirmeyah told him, “Let the master come and teach.” He answered, “My heart is weak; I cannot.” “Let the master say aggadah.” He answered, “Thus said Rabbi Yochanan …”: Taanit 7a. Ein Yaakov reverses it: Rabbi Zeira told Yirmeyah, “Let the master come and teach ….” The Gemara’s reading appears right, for Zeira commonly weakened from study. Chullin 44b: when gifts were sent he did not accept; when invited he went, saying, “They honor themselves through me.” Rabbah and Zeira held a Purim meal together and became intoxicated. Rabbah arose and slaughtered Zeira; next day he prayed and revived him: Megillah 7b. In Zeira’s days they imposed a decree, including a ban on fasting. Zeira said, “Let us accept it upon ourselves, and when the decree is annulled let us observe it”: Taanit 8b. Zeira said: Israel’s daughters were stringent, observing seven clean days even for a mustard-sized blood drop; Megillah. Zeira said, “This matter was asked”—it should read “conveyed indirectly,” as in N.Y.—“to me at Rav Hamnuna’s house, and is worth all my learning: sneezing in prayer is a good sign”: Berakhot 24b. Rashi: it is weighty and dear to him because he often sneezed. He expounded in Mechoza that a convert may marry a mamzeret; they pelted him with etrogim: Asarah Yuchasin 73a. Jerusalem Talmud,end of Hazahav: Zeira traded in flax. Rashi,Sukkah 25,end of side b: this was a case such as marrying on the eve of the festival. Zeira went up to the Land before Rabbi Abba (see his entry). On arriving he ate meat slaughtered beyond the boundary according to Rav and Shmuel. They asked, “Are you not from Rav and Shmuel’s place?” He answered …: Chullin 18b; see Rav Yosef. Niddah 23a: Yirmeyah asked Zeira about an animal in a woman’s womb whose father accepted betrothal for it. Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: Yirmeyah brought Zeira this far toward laughter, but he did not laugh, because one may not fill his mouth with laughter, and Zeira was stricter still. Tosafot,Chullin 13a, says Yirmeyah was Zeira’s colleague, as proved by that Niddah passage, and Zeira was Rav Yehudah’s student. Tosafot,Gittin 11b, likewise says Zeira was Yehudah’s student and greater than Yirmeyah (see Rav Huna). Yirmeyah told him …; he answered, “Did I not say, ‘Let him go …’?” Zeira said, “We held this matter, and Rabbi Chanina threw an axe into it”: Rosh Hashanah 13a. Rav Chisda said: Zeira said: Rav Yirmeyah said in Rav’s name,Horayot 6a. Menachot 81b: Yirmeyah sat before Zeira and said, “They taught only ….” He told him, “My teacher, do you say this?” “Sat before him” suggests Yirmeyah was Zeira’s student (see the rules); “My teacher,do you say this?” suggests Rav Yirmeyah was his teacher. Shabbat 7;Pesachim 40a: Zeira said in Yirmeyah’s name. Shabbat 71a: Yirmeyah asked Zeira. When Zeira died, the eulogist opened, “The land of Shinar conceived and bore”—he was born in Babylonia—“the land of the gazelle [the Land of Israel] raised him”; he died in Tiberias: Moed Katan 25b.

F) Rabbi Abba: Moed Katan 22a; Chullin 50a: Rabbi Abba’s colleague learned from him—who is that? Rabbi Zeira. Zeira said, “I heard from Rabbi Abba; without Rabbi Abba of Akko I would have forgotten” (see his entry). He told Rabbi Abba bar Pappa to ask Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi (see his entry). In Rabbi Abba bar Yirmeyah’s name. He reported Rabbi Abba bar Zemina. Rabbi Abba bar Chiyya bar Abba was his colleague. Rabbi Assi met Zeira and said, “I asked Rabbi Abba bar Mammal” (see his entry); Abba bar Mammal disagreed with him and died during Zeira’s lifetime. He said to Rabbi Abba bar Kahana. Zeira asked Abbahu: “What if the likeness of a donkey descended from heaven?” He replied, “Foolish yarod”—Rashi: a foolish tannin; see Chavvot Yair’s responsa 152, that he called him this in praise, at length there—“nothing impure descends from heaven”: Sanhedrin 59,end of side b. Zeira said, “I saw Abbahu”: Shabbat 40b, 41a. Rabbi Avin’s father recited before him. Rabbi Tzafra’s father asked Zeira. Abaye said to him: Chullin 45b; Abaye: Zevachim 5a; Menachot 25a. Zeira made an eruv for Rabbi Chiyya’s town. Abaye asked, “Why does the master do this?” He answered, “Its elders told me Rabbi Chiyya bar Assi made an eruv …”: Keitzad Meabberin 59b. Abaye said in Zeira’s name: Berakhot 31a. Avimi bar Pappa said to him. Rabbi Avin bar Chiyya asked him. He asked Rabbi Avin bar Kahana; and Rabbi Avin. He said to Rabbi Avina. In Rabbi Adda bar Achva’s name. Ahavah was his son. He reported Rabbi Oshaya: Ketubbot 79,end of side a. Rav Acha was his son. Rabbi Acha reported Zeira; Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov reported Zeira. Rabbi Ilai. Zeira said, “From our master’s words we learn”—Rashbam: Rabbi Elazar,Bava Batra 82b. When he went up he found Rabbi Elazar—ben Pedat,Rashi—Niddah 48a. In Eruvin 66a, Elazar wondered about it. Zeira asked, “What is the wondering?” Rav Sheshet said, “Does a great man like Zeira not know what Elazar wonders about? His difficulty is Shmuel,his teacher,who said ….” He asked Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Ammi bar Chiyya. He told Rabbi Assi, “Did my teacher not hear …?” He answered, “This scholar resembles someone who has not learned the teaching”: Bava Batra 84b. Niddah 53b: “He asked Rabbi Yose” is a scribal error for Assi, as in Rashi. He asked Assi: Shabbat 130b; there 71a, Zeira asked “Rabbi Assi”—this is how it should read, also in newer editions; see there, for Assi was his teacher. Zeira said Rav Assi’s view is reasonable: Beitzah 4b. Zeira said to Rabbi Assi: Kiddushin 39a. Rav Assi (see Rabbi Mallukh). When he went up he found Assi saying: Avodah Zarah 16b. He said to Rav Bibi (see Rabbi Mallukh); Rav Bibi bar Avin. Zeira wondered: “What has Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet to do with Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba?” Berakhot 38b. He met Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet: Ketubbot 77a. He sat behind Rav Giddel, and Giddel before Rav Huna (see his entry). Zeira said, “When I was in Huna’s house …; when we came to Yehudah’s house …”: Berakhot 39a. He reported Rav Huna: Bava Kamma 9,end of side a. Rav Hamnuna told him, “Do not sit back on your heels” (see above). Rav Hamnuna Zuta was his colleague. He reported Rav Zevid. A son of Rav Zevid visited him (see his entry). Rabbi Chaggai asked him. He reported Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi. Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin asked him; Chiyya bar Ammi; Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba [רב אבא in source, see his entry]; Rabbi Chiyya bar Pappa before him; Rabbi Chama bar Ukva. Rabbi Zeira said in Rabbi Chanina’s name. He told Rav Chisda, “Let the master come and teach.” He answered, “I do not know even grace after meals: I visited the exilarch’s house and recited grace; Rav Sheshet raised his neck against me like a snake”: Berakhot 49a. He reported Rav Chisda: Beitzah 33b; Ketubbot 95a; Zevachim 109b. Rav Chisda reported Zeira (see above). He asked Rav Yehudah: Berakhot 48a; Yehudah was his teacher. Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi; Rabbi Yehudah bar Ammi (see above); Rabbi Yehoshua bar Zeydal. He reported Rabbi Yochanan: Berakhot 47b. Yochanan told him: Gittin 40,beginning of side a. Rabbi Yochanan ben Elyakim. Rabbi Yonah reported Zeira. He saw Rabbi Yose bar Chanina and asked in a dream beside whom he sat in the heavenly academy (see Rabbi Chiyya). He disagrees with Rabbi Yosef bar Chama. Rav Yosef was angry with him. Rabbah and Rav Yosef sat behind Zeira, and Zeira before Ulla: Pesachim 37b. He asked Rabbi Yannai, and Yannai reported Zeira. In the name of one of Yannai’s house. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha in his name. He told Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi, “Perhaps my teacher did not hear ….” He replied, “This scholar resembles one who has not learned the teaching”: Chullin 5b; Eruvin 46a. In Gittin 39,end of side a, Zeira asked, “Did you hear explicitly”—Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s statement,Rashi—“and the master did not hear?” Rabbi Yaakov bar Bat Yaakov. He reported Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha. He asked Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachman; spoke to Rabbi Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta. Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba. Rabbi Yirmeyah (see above). He reported Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba. Rabbi Mallukh said to him; Mar Keshisha son of Rav Chisda said to him. Mar son of Ravina; Rav Mattanah. He reported Rav Nachman. Rav Natan bar Tuvyah (see above). He told Rabbi Simon, “Let the master rebuke the members of the exilarch’s household.” Rav Safra said: he asked Ulla and sat before him (see above). He reported Mar Ukva. In Rabbi Pedayah’s name. He said to Rabbi Pedat,son of Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat. He reported Rav: Shabbat 21,beginning of side b, 130b; Eruvin 91b; Sotah 18a; Chelek 100,end of side b. Bekhorot 39b: Rabbi Zeira said in Rav’s name; Zevachim 25b instead has Rabbi. Rava said, “I and the lion of the group”—who is that? Rabbi Zeira—Bava Batra 88a. He visited the exilarch’s house; Zeira addressed Rava as “master”: Berakhot 42a. They disagree in Beitzah 8b; Shabbat 74,end of side b,and 75b,they both say. Rava created a man and sent him to Zeira. Rava said of him, “Who is this who takes no care for his flour?” Sukkah 54a. Rava,Zeira,Rabbah son of Rav Chanan,and Abaye sat: Eruvin 92a. There,end of side b,Tosafot writes we read “Rabbah and Zeira sat.” He reported Rabbah bar Yirmeyah; Rava bar Zemoni. Rabbah (see above). He reported Rabbah bar Sheila. Rabbah bar Mattanah was his colleague. Rabbah son of Rav Chanan (see above). He reported Rabbah bar Sheilta. Ravin bar Chinena; Rami bar Tamra; Rabbi Shaul in his time; Shmuel bar Ammi. Two great men of the generation,Zeira and Rabbi Shmuel bar [Rav] Yitzchak: Gittin 23b. He reported Shmuel: Eruvin 29b, 81a; Ketubbot 96a; Gittin 35a; Chullin 8a. Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi. He reported Resh Lakish: Pesachim 72b. Rav Sheshet (see above).
